S14.01.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account and a file on the phone
S14.01.note: The File card is shown only when the mode is AGI Cloud (AddToChatSheet.tsx:720); the sheet has no File card in on-device mode.
steps: On the Chat screen, switch the mode toggle to AGI Cloud.
Tap the + button labelled Add to chat at the left of the message box.
Tap the File card in the sheet titled Add to Chat.
In the phone's file chooser, pick a PDF or text file.
Look at the composer: the file should appear as a chip, and after sending the message the file should be attached to it.
S14.01.where: Chat screen > Add to chat (+) > File (AGI Cloud mode only)

S14.04.needs: a phone with a camera; an account that has the camera capability (the Camera card is hidden otherwise)
S14.04.note: The Camera card depends on the canUseCamera capability (AddToChatSheet.tsx:697), so a tester on an account without it will not see it.
steps: On the Chat screen, tap the + button labelled Add to chat.
Tap the Camera card in the sheet titled Add to Chat.
If asked, allow camera access; take a photo with the camera screen.
Look at the composer: the photo should appear as a thumbnail chip, ready to send.
S14.04.where: Chat screen > Add to chat (+) > Camera

S14.05.needs: a phone with at least one photo in the library
steps: On the Chat screen, tap the + button labelled Add to chat.
Tap the Photos card in the sheet titled Add to Chat.
In the photo library, tap one photo, then confirm the picker.
Look at the composer: the chosen photo should appear as a thumbnail chip.
S14.05.where: Chat screen > Add to chat (+) > Photos

S14.10.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account with at least one image or file already in its Library
S14.10.note: The section appears only when Library items exist; it is hidden in an empty Library.
steps: On the Chat screen, switch the mode to AGI Cloud.
Tap the + button labelled Add to chat.
Look for the Attach from Library section in the sheet and tap a file row (its label reads Attach <file name> from Library).
Look at the composer: the Library file should appear as an attachment chip.
S14.10.where: Chat screen > Add to chat (+) > Attach from Library (tap a file row)

S14.15.needs: several photos on the phone, and for the File part an AGI Cloud account and several files
S14.15.note: The photo picker is multi-select (allowsMultipleSelection true) and the file chooser sets multiple: true.
steps: Tap the + button labelled Add to chat, then tap Photos.
In the photo picker, tap two or more photos, then confirm.
Look at the composer: every chosen photo should appear as its own chip.
Repeat with AGI Cloud mode and File, choosing several files, and check that each one is attached.
S14.15.where: Chat screen > Add to chat (+) > Photos (select several); AGI Cloud mode > Add to chat (+) > File (select several)

S14.16.needs: a phone with a photo in the library
steps: Tap the + button labelled Add to chat, then tap Photos.
Pick one photo and confirm.
Look at the message box area: the photo should show as a square picture (about 72 by 72) before sending.
S14.16.where: Chat screen > Add to chat (+) > Photos

S14.17.needs: an AGI Cloud account and one PDF, one spreadsheet and one code file
S14.17.note: Other kinds show the words Presentation, Document, Text or File (AttachmentPreview.tsx:105-111).
steps: Switch to AGI Cloud, tap Add to chat (+), then tap the File card.
Pick a PDF, then a spreadsheet (for example .csv or .xlsx), then a code file (for example .py).
Look at each chip: under the file name it should show the kind word: PDF, Spreadsheet or Code.
S14.17.where: Chat screen > Add to chat (+) > File (AGI Cloud mode)

S14.18.needs: an AGI Cloud account and a non-image file
steps: Switch to AGI Cloud, tap Add to chat (+), then tap File.
Pick a non-image file such as a PDF.
Look at the chip: it should show the file name and, under it, the kind and size (for example PDF and a size in KB or MB).
S14.18.where: Chat screen > Add to chat (+) > File (AGI Cloud mode)

S14.19.needs: an AGI Cloud account and a large file
S14.19.note: The progress label text is in apps/mobile/src/features/chat/upload/uploadLifecycle.ts:46 and is not drawn on screen; only the bar is visible.
steps: Switch to AGI Cloud, tap Add to chat (+), then tap File.
Pick a large file (several megabytes) so the upload lasts a few seconds.
While it uploads, look at the bottom edge of the chip: a thin progress bar fills up.
Compare with Expected: the chip shows progress while the upload runs. The percentage (Uploading NN%) is only in the screen-reader label, not printed on the chip.
S14.19.where: Chat screen > AGI Cloud mode > Add to chat (+) > File

S14.22.note: No visible 'ready' wording was found in AttachmentPreview.tsx; the word Uploaded only appears in a screen-reader label.
steps: Switch to AGI Cloud, tap Add to chat (+), then pick a photo under Photos.
Watch the chip while it uploads (progress bar).
When the bar disappears, check the chip has no Retry or Cancel overlay and the Send button is not held.
Compare with Expected: the code shows no visible Ready or Uploaded word, so judge whether the chip alone makes ready clear.
S14.22.where: Chat screen > AGI Cloud mode > Add to chat (+) > Photos or File, then wait for the upload

S14.23.needs: an AGI Cloud account and a long document
S14.23.note: The notice is shown only for the AGI Cloud path (streaming header); on-device reading adds the text to the model input instead.
steps: Switch to AGI Cloud, tap Add to chat (+), then tap File.
Pick a long text or document file that is larger than the readable limit.
Type a short question and send.
Look under your sent message: a grey line should say Only part of <file name> was read because it is too long to read in full.
S14.23.where: Chat screen > AGI Cloud mode > Add to chat (+) > File, then send; read the line under your sent message

S14.24.needs: an AGI Cloud account and a file the chat refuses
S14.24.note: The chooser only offers types listed in services/docParser.ts, so a refused type may not be selectable; the alert text is in apps/mobile/src/features/chat/utils/attachmentValidation.ts:123.
steps: Switch to AGI Cloud, tap Add to chat (+), then tap File.
Pick a file type the chat cannot read (for example an executable or an unsupported archive, if the chooser lets you pick it).
Look for the alert titled Attachment not added: it should name the file and say it is not a supported file type.
S14.24.where: Chat screen > AGI Cloud mode > Add to chat (+) > File

S14.25.note: The notice text is written only into the input sent to the model (apps/mobile/services/attachmentContext.ts:45), so no app-drawn notice was found; the File card that could attach a PDF is shown only in AGI Cloud mode (AddToChatSheet.tsx:720), where the password check runs on the server, which is not in this app's code. Searched apps/mobile for ENCRYPTED_PDF and password protected.

S14.26.needs: an AGI Cloud account and a way to switch the network off and on
steps: Switch to AGI Cloud, turn Wi-Fi and mobile data off, then tap Add to chat (+) and pick a photo.
Wait until the chip shows a failed state with a Retry overlay.
Turn the network back on and tap Retry on the chip.
Look at the chip: the upload should start again and the Retry overlay should go away when it finishes.
S14.26.where: Chat screen > AGI Cloud mode > Add to chat (+) > Photos (upload fails), then tap Retry on the chip

S14.27.needs: an AGI Cloud account and a large file
steps: Switch to AGI Cloud, tap Add to chat (+), then tap File and pick a large file.
While the progress bar is moving, tap the small X on the chip's corner (screen reader label: Cancel upload of <file name>).
Look at the chip: it should disappear and the upload should stop.
S14.27.where: Chat screen > AGI Cloud mode > Add to chat (+) > File, then tap the small X on the uploading chip

S14.28.needs: a phone with at least two photos
steps: Tap Add to chat (+), then tap Photos and pick two photos.
Tap the small X at the top corner of one chip (screen reader label: Remove <file name>).
Look at the composer: that chip should disappear.
Send the message and check the sent message shows only the other photo.
S14.28.where: Chat screen > Add to chat (+) > Photos, then tap the small X on the chip

S14.31.needs: a phone with a photo in the library
S14.31.note: Duplicates are matched by attachment identity; a newly taken camera photo has a new identity, so it is not treated as a duplicate.
steps: Tap Add to chat (+), then tap Photos and pick one photo.
Open Add to chat (+) again, tap Photos, and pick the same photo again.
Look for an alert titled Already attached that names the file and says Each file is attached once.
Check the composer shows the photo only once.
S14.31.where: Chat screen > Add to chat (+) > Photos (pick the same photo twice)

S14.32.needs: an AGI Cloud account and one file the chat refuses
S14.32.note: Per-file reasons are built in apps/mobile/src/features/chat/utils/attachmentValidation.ts; a failed upload shows Retry on that chip (AttachmentPreview.tsx:392) rather than a named error.
steps: Switch to AGI Cloud, tap Add to chat (+), then tap File.
Pick one acceptable file and one refused file together.
Look for the alert Attachment not added: it should name the refused file in quotes and give the reason.
Check that the accepted file still appears as a chip.
S14.32.where: Chat screen > AGI Cloud mode > Add to chat (+) > File (pick several files, one refused)

S14.33.needs: an AGI Cloud account and three files, one refused
steps: Switch to AGI Cloud, tap Add to chat (+), then tap File.
Pick three files, with at least one the chat refuses.
Look for one alert titled Some attachments not added that lists each refused file with its reason.
Check that the accepted files appear as chips in the composer.
S14.33.where: Chat screen > AGI Cloud mode > Add to chat (+) > File (pick three or more files, one refused)

labels.text: Uploaded to AGI Cloud and kept in your Library until you delete them.

S14.34.needs: an AGI Cloud account; a temporary chat for the second check
S14.34.note: The on-device-mode caption (AddToChatSheet.tsx:131) says nothing about keeping files, so in on-device mode the explanation is missing.
steps: Tap Add to chat (+) with AGI Cloud mode on.
Read the grey line under the Add to Chat title: it should say Uploaded to AGI Cloud and kept in your Library until you delete them.
Open a temporary chat and tap Add to chat (+) again; the line should say Kept out of your Library and deleted with this temporary chat.
Compare with Expected: whether and how long files are kept.
S14.34.where: Chat screen > Add to chat (+) (read the caption under the Add to Chat title)

labels.text: retake it with the in-app camera

S14.36.needs: an AGI Cloud account and a HEIC photo on the phone
S14.36.note: HEIC photos may be converted before this check (apps/mobile/src/features/media/image-normalization), so the alert may not appear; the on-device Office-file alert (switch to AGI Cloud for Office files) is not reachable from the sheet because the File card is hidden in on-device mode.
steps: Switch to AGI Cloud, tap Add to chat (+), then tap Photos.
Pick a HEIC photo from the library.
Look for the alert Attachment not added: it should say AGI Cloud cannot read the HEIC photo and to retake it with the in-app camera.
Compare with Expected: the alert names the alternative (retake with the camera).
S14.36.where: Chat screen > AGI Cloud mode > Add to chat (+) > Photos (pick a HEIC photo)
